q: Which type of element usually forms an acidic oxide?
explain: Non-metals form acidic oxides while metals form basic oxides.

q: A student adds copper(II) oxide to warm dilute sulfuric acid until no more dissolves. What is the next step?
options: filter the mixture to remove the excess solid
explain: Excess copper(II) oxide is removed by filtration, leaving copper(II) sulfate solution as the filtrate.

q: Which statement about bases and alkalis is correct?
options: All bases dissolve in water to form alkalis.
An alkali is a base that dissolves in water.
An alkali is any oxide of a non-metal.
A base is an acid that has been diluted.
explain: Bases are metal oxides or hydroxides; only the soluble ones are called alkalis, so every alkali is a base but not every base is an alkali.

q: Which salt is insoluble in water?
explain: Sulfates are soluble except those of barium, calcium and lead.

q: What is meant by a hydrated substance?
options: a substance chemically combined with water
a substance with water on its surface
explain: A hydrated substance has water molecules as part of its crystal structure.

q: Which compound is classified differently from the other three?
explain: ZnO is amphoteric, whereas CaO, CuO and MgO are basic oxides.

q: Four solutions have the pH values shown. Which has the highest concentration of hydrogen ions?
explain: The lower the pH, the higher the hydrogen ion concentration, so pH 1 is the most acidic.

q: Which metal does not produce hydrogen when added to dilute hydrochloric acid?
explain: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does not react with dilute acids.

q: In the reaction HCl + NH₃ → NH₄Cl, what is the role of HCl?
options: It accepts a proton from NH₃.
It donates a proton to NH₃.
It accepts an electron from NH₃.
explain: HCl transfers H⁺ to the lone pair on NH₃, so HCl is the proton donor (acid).

q: Which indicator is colourless in dilute acid and blue in aqueous alkali?
explain: Thymolphthalein is colourless in acids and blue in alkalis. Litmus is red/blue and methyl orange red/yellow.

q: Which equation represents the neutralisation reaction between an acid and an alkali?
explain: Neutralisation is the combination of hydrogen ions from the acid with hydroxide ions from the alkali to form water.

q: What is the percentage by mass of water in CuSO₄•5H₂O? (Ar: Cu = 64, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
Which method is suitable for preparing insoluble barium sulfate?
options: adding excess barium to dilute sulfuric acid
titrating barium hydroxide with hydrochloric acid
precipitation by mixing aqueous barium chloride and aqueous sodium sulfate
adding excess barium oxide to dilute nitric acid
explain: An insoluble salt is made by mixing two soluble salts that contain its ions, followed by filtering, washing and drying.

q: Which method is used to prepare sodium chloride crystals from hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodium hydroxide?
options: adding excess sodium metal and filtering
titration followed by evaporation and crystallisation
adding excess sodium carbonate and filtering
explain: Both reactants are soluble, so exact amounts are found by titration, then the solution is evaporated and crystallised.

q: A salt solution is warmed until about half the water has evaporated, then left to cool. Why is the solution not heated to dryness?
options: Crystals form on cooling and heating to dryness could decompose the salt.
The salt would evaporate with the water.
Heating to dryness would make the salt insoluble.
Crystals only form when the solution is hot.
explain: Heating until a saturated solution forms, then cooling lets crystals grow. Complete evaporation can spoil or decompose hydrated salts.

q: Which statement describes an amphoteric oxide?
options: It reacts only with acids to form a salt and water.
It reacts with both acids and bases to form a salt and water.
It reacts only with bases to form a salt and water.
It does not react with acids or bases.
explain: An amphoteric oxide has both acidic and basic behaviour, reacting with acids and with bases.

q: A white solid forms when aqueous lead(II) nitrate is added to aqueous potassium chloride. Which equation, with state symbols, represents the reaction?
explain: Lead chloride is insoluble. Two Cl⁻ ions balance one Pb²⁺, so the equation is Pb²⁺ + 2Cl⁻ → PbCl₂.

q: Which ionic equation represents the formation of silver chloride when aqueous silver nitrate is added to aqueous sodium chloride?
explain: Only silver and chloride ions combine to form the insoluble solid. Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ are spectator ions.

q: What colour does universal indicator paper turn in a strongly acidic solution such as pH 1?
explain: Universal indicator is red in strongly acidic solutions, green when neutral and purple in strongly alkaline solutions.

q: Which of these is a base?
explain: Bases are oxides or hydroxides of metals. Magnesium oxide is a metal oxide; the other three are non-metal compounds.

q: In the preparation of a soluble salt from an insoluble base, why is the base added in excess?
options: to make the reaction go faster
to make sure all the acid is used up
to make the salt purer after crystallising
explain: Adding excess solid ensures all the acid is neutralised; the unreacted solid is then filtered off.

q: Which sequence of steps gives crystals of zinc nitrate from excess zinc carbonate and dilute nitric acid?
options: evaporate the acid, add carbonate, then filter
add carbonate, cool, filter, then add more acid
add carbonate until no more dissolves, filter, evaporate part of the water, cool
filter the acid, add indicator, boil to dryness
explain: Excess carbonate ensures neutralisation. The unreacted solid is filtered off, the filtrate is partly evaporated and then cooled to crystallise.

q: Copper(II) oxide does not dissolve in aqueous sodium hydroxide but dissolves in dilute nitric acid. How is copper(II) oxide classified?
explain: It reacts only with acids, not with alkalis, so it is purely basic.

q: What is the mass of 0.0100 mol of CuSO₄•5H₂O? (Ar: Cu = 64, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
Which statement about metal oxides and non-metal oxides is correct?
options: Metal oxides are generally acidic and non-metal oxides generally basic.
Metal oxides are generally basic and non-metal oxides generally acidic.
explain: The character of an oxide is linked to whether the element is metallic or non-metallic.

q: Which statement about the preparation of a soluble salt by titration is correct?
options: The salt is formed by precipitation.
An excess of insoluble base is added.
An indicator is used to find the volumes needed for neutralisation.
explain: Titration uses an indicator to find the end-point, giving exactly the volumes needed for a pure solution of the salt.

q: 2.50 g of CuSO₄•5H₂O is heated until all the water is removed. What is the mass of anhydrous CuSO₄ left? (Ar: Cu = 64, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
explain: Mr of CuSO₄•5H₂O = 250 and Mr of CuSO₄ = 160. 2.50 × 160 ÷ 250 = 1.60 g.

q: What is the product (other than water) when zinc oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
explain: ZnO + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂O. This is typical of a base reacting with an acid.

q: Which statement about precipitation is correct?
options: It always requires an acid and an alkali.
It forms an insoluble salt when two solutions are mixed.
explain: A precipitate forms when ions of an insoluble compound meet in solution.

q: Iron(III) oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid. What does this indicate about iron(III) oxide?
explain: Reaction with an acid to give a salt and water is characteristic of a basic oxide, which is a metal oxide.
